mistakes: No plan setups today (calendar only), so this review covers the pasted Opening Range trades and web price reports, not OANDA fills.
News filter broken: all five T1 trades (6:40–6:47am) were USD pairs entered before the 07:00 USD UoM Consumer Sentiment release, which blocked every USD pair. All five stopped out (−5.06R).
AUD/USD T2 had no take profit and was closed by hand, and its stop was 5 pips tighter than the signal's. It finished well (+2.96R), but that isn't set and forget.

Daily loss limit: the five T1 losses add up to −5.06R. At 2% per R that is about −10%, well past the −4% limit. Close times aren't in the block, so it can't be told whether the 7:14am AUD/USD T2 entry came after the limit was hit.
Two T2 signals that hit +2R targets after the news were missed (USD/CAD and NZD/USD).
lessons: Repeat: Execution on the T1 signals was clean: signal price, signal stop and target, and each loss held to about −1R. Taking AUD/USD T2 once the news cleared was the right signal.

Improve tomorrow: Check the news blocks before the first entry. When a red-folder USD event is at 07:00, skip T1 on USD pairs and wait for T2 after the release. Give every trade the signal's stop and target, and stop for the day at −2R closed (−4%).

Most profit: T2 paid and T1 didn't. All 7 T1 signals stopped (−7R) while T2 hit 3 targets (AUD/USD, USD/CAD, NZD/USD +2R each), stopped 2 (USD/JPY, USD/CHF) and 2 were still open, for +4R so far. Skipping the T1 trades inside the news block and taking the three T2 winners at their targets would have made about +6R instead of −2.10R.
review.gradingAudit: No plan setups to audit today. Execution: 5 A, 0 B, 1 C across 6 trades, all closed, net −2.10R. The A grades are fair for following the signals, but they don't capture the news-filter break: all five A trades were entered before the 07:00 USD release. The one C trade was the only winner (+2.96R).
